Subject: Tuesday reading club — new numbers ahead of the review

Dear Niamh,

I wanted to write before the review meeting on Wednesday 18 November, as there has been a lovely change in the Tuesday reading club’s attendance since the early weeks. I also need to tell you about an invitation I gave a local reporter without checking with you first.

I understand from your email of 30 October that the club is to be paused from January because of low attendance and the increase in the hall insurance. I know the insurance is a real consideration, whatever our numbers, but I hope the latest figures might give us grounds to reconsider the pause.

We had five children most weeks in September, nine by mid-October, and fourteen last Tuesday, 3 November. After running the club since September 2025, it is a great pleasure to see the upstairs meeting room at Knocknacarra library filling up on Tuesdays. Our 3.30 to 4.45 session is beginning to feel like the little reading club we hoped it would become.

There are small things happening that the numbers alone don’t quite capture. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October, and the older girl now reads to her younger sister in English at the end of each session. One boy who wouldn’t open a book in September asked last week if he could take two home. You can imagine how delighted I was with that.

We have also had a very generous donation from Declan Moran, who owns Salthill Book Nook: 120 books, mostly for the six-to-nine age group, with a good few as Gaeilge. It gives the children much more choice, just when we have more of them coming through the door.

I would be very sorry to see us stop just as things are taking off. Could you bring these new figures to the review on the 18th and reconsider the January pause? I appreciate that attendance is only part of the decision, but I wanted you to have the fuller picture beforehand.

Now, about the reporter. I met Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier at the farmers’ market and got carried away telling her about the club. I said, “Come along any Tuesday,” and agreed she could come and take photographs. She would now like to visit on Tuesday 24 November with a photographer.

I was wrong not to check with you first, plain and simple. I know that photographs of the children require your sign-off and the parental consent forms. I wanted you to hear directly from me what I had said, rather than have an enquiry from Orla arrive out of the blue.

I’ll ring her and put the visit on hold until you’ve decided whether it should go ahead. If you do approve it, I’m very happy to collect the parental consent forms myself, following your guidance. The coverage could be wonderful for the club, but only if it is done properly. Please don’t feel that my invitation commits you to anything.

Thank you for considering all of this, Niamh. I’m thrilled with the children’s progress and hopeful that we can keep it going after Christmas.

Warm wishes,
[Your name]
